elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 15.5(b): "services performed by Array under this Agreement, including Development and Manufacturing activities, will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner".

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: New 15.5(a): "Materials supplied to Ono will conform in all material respects to their specifications" — Materials are the tangible deliverable Array supplies and specifications are their governing documentation; no software exists under this pharma license/supply agreement.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 15.5(a) sets ninety (90) days following delivery, not twelve (12) months.
15.5(b) sets thirty (30) days following performance, not 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 15.5: "at Ono's election, repair, replacement or re-performance".
15.5: "or a refund of the amounts paid for the non-conforming Materials or services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: 15.2 gives only Effective-Date status/IP representations (e.g., ownership of Array Patents in 15.2(j)); the inserted 15.5 contains no ongoing compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in 15.2, 15.4 or the inserted 15.5. Commercially inapplicable to pharmaceutical Materials, but the element is nonetheless unaddressed in operative language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 15.5(a) warrants Materials "conform in all material respects to their specifications for ninety (90) days following delivery". The Agreement licenses and supplies pharmaceutical Materials, not software, so the deliverable-to-specification warranty is the direct analogue; this is a conformance warranty on the item Array actually supplies, not a report/output/service dressed up as software.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 15.5(b) warrants Array's services for "thirty (30) days following performance" to a professional and workmanlike standard — meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 15.5 remedy sentence expressly includes "repair, replacement or re-performance".
15.5 remedy sentence expressly includes "a refund of the amounts paid for the non-conforming Materials or services".

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: Article 15 contains only as-of-Effective-Date status/IP representations (15.2) plus a broad disclaimer of merchantability and fitness (15.4), and product conformity is deferred to a future Supply/Quality Agreement (9.4(b)(i)), which is an agreement to agree with no period or remedy today. There is no conformance warranty, duration or remedy in the current text, so the fallback fails on material terms.
Fallback level is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (90 days Materials-to-specifications, 30 days services, repair/replacement/re-performance, refund).

Preferred level is not met: the software/deliverable period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty. If pushing to preferred, extend 15.5(a) to twelve (12) months, 15.5(b) to ninety (90) days, and add an ongoing "Array shall perform in compliance with all applicable laws" warranty.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise new Section 15.5 with no survival tail, no expense allocation, no procedural mechanics and no extra damages categories. The clarifiers "including Development and Manufacturing activities" and "amounts paid" are justified because neither "Services" nor "Fees" is a defined term in this collaboration agreement, so the warranty would otherwise lack determinate scope and a refund measure. Nothing was deleted from 15.1-15.4.

Intent preserved: 15.4 opens with "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement," so the new express warranty in 15.5 survives the disclaimer without amending it; the Effective-Date representations, the future Supply Agreement mechanics in 9.4(b)(i) and all other allocations are untouched and non-contradictory.

Drafting nit to tighten (not an element failure): "their specifications" has no present referent until the Supply Agreement is executed. Consider "the specifications for such Materials set forth in the Supply Agreement or otherwise agreed by the Parties in writing" so the conformance standard cannot be argued to be indeterminate.

Second nit: the model remedy is at Vendor's option; 15.5 puts the election with Ono. That is a customer-favourable ask beyond the checklist minimum and is the most likely point Array pushes back on — be prepared to concede "at Array's option" without losing the fallback.
